sentences.text:
Dated this the 7th day of February, 2025 Petitioner is the sole accused in Crime No.979 of 2024 registered at the Kollam West Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 370 and 420 of IPC.
2.
The crime is registered on the allegation that the accused collected Rs.1,50,000/- from the defacto complainant, promising to secure him a job in Cambodia.
Though defacto complainant was taken to Cambodia, there he was illegally confined and abused physically and mentally.
3. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the dispute involved in all other crimes have been settled and further proceedings quashed by this Court.

It is further submitted that even though this Court, by order dated 02.12.2024, had directed the petitioner to 2025:KER:12713 surrender in the lower court and seek bail, his client was unable to surrender within the time granted, by reason of her involvement in another crime.

4. The petitioner having settled the dispute by paying the amount due to the defacto complainant,
she need not be compelled to surrender before the trial court.
5. Learned Counsel for the 3rd respondent also submitted that the dispute is settled and his client has no grievance against the petitioner.
6. Learned Public Prosecutor points out that the petitioner is involved in 4 other similar crimes.

7. Having considered the gravity of the offences alleged and having perused the affidavit, contents of which are vouched to be true and voluntary by the Counsel for the 3rd respondent, I am satisfied that no public interest is involved in this matter and the 2025:KER:12713 dispute has been settled amicably.
In view of the settlement, there is no possibility of the criminal proceedings ending in conviction.

Being so, in view of the legal position set out by the Honourable Supreme Court in Madan Mohan Abbot v State of Punjab [(2008) 4 SCC 582] and Gian Singh v State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303], there is no impediment in granting the relief.
